original_question: Is the class S1(BOmega,BGamma) preserved by finite powers?
target_in_paper: Section 6.2, Problem 6.4: "Is S1(BΩ, BΓ) preserved by finite powers?" ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=4751a09b2173c9726c9936b8b6ae7acd3ae230b3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the exact property and the exact preservation question asked in the paper; it is essentially the official formulation of Problem 6.4 with only notation-level stand-alone details omitted. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=4751a09b2173c9726c9936b8b6ae7acd3ae230b3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper is working with sets of reals (more generally, the chapter restricts to the part of the theory dealing with sets of real numbers), so the ambient objects are subspaces X ⊆ ℝ, not arbitrary spaces without context. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=4751a09b2173c9726c9936b8b6ae7acd3ae230b3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The selection principle S1(A,B) should be defined explicitly: for each sequence {Un : n ∈ ℕ} of members of A, choose Un ∈ Un so that {Un : n ∈ ℕ} is a member of B. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=4751a09b2173c9726c9936b8b6ae7acd3ae230b3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The symbols BΩ and BΓ should be unpacked: they are the families of countable Borel ω-covers and countable Borel γ-covers, respectively. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=4751a09b2173c9726c9936b8b6ae7acd3ae230b3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

A Borel ω-cover should be spelled out as a countable family of Borel subsets of X such that X itself is not a member of the cover and every finite F ⊆ X is contained in some member of the cover. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=4751a09b2173c9726c9936b8b6ae7acd3ae230b3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

A Borel γ-cover should be spelled out as a countably infinite family of Borel subsets of X such that each x ∈ X belongs to all but finitely many members of the cover. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=4751a09b2173c9726c9936b8b6ae7acd3ae230b3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

"Preserved by finite powers" should be made explicit as: for every positive integer n, if X satisfies S1(BΩ,BΓ), then X^n with the product topology also satisfies S1(BΩ,BΓ). The quantifier over all finite n is implicit in the paper’s wording. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=4751a09b2173c9726c9936b8b6ae7acd3ae230b3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
refined_question: For a set of reals X, let BΩ(X) denote the family of countable Borel ω-covers of X, meaning countable families U of Borel subsets of X such that X ∉ U and every finite F ⊆ X is contained in some U ∈ U; and let BΓ(X) denote the family of countably infinite Borel γ-covers of X, meaning countable Borel covers U of X such that each x ∈ X belongs to all but finitely many members of U. Writing S1(BΩ,BΓ) for the property that for every sequence (Un)n∈ℕ with each Un ∈ BΩ(X), one can choose Un ∈ Un so that {Un : n ∈ ℕ} ∈ BΓ(X), is it true that whenever X ⊆ ℝ satisfies S1(BΩ,BΓ), then for every positive integer n the finite power X^n, with the product topology, also satisfies S1(BΩ,BΓ)? ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=4751a09b2173c9726c9936b8b6ae7acd3ae230b3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s Problem 6.4 exactly. Section 1 supplies the formal meaning of S1(A,B) and of ω- and γ-covers; Section 2 introduces the Borel cover notation B, BΩ, and BΓ for sets of reals; and Section 6.2 states the question verbatim as Problem 6.4, with the nearby remark that the analogous finite-power questions for the other Borel classes have negative answers. The paper does not present a separate equivalent reformulation of Problem 6.4 itself, so the sharpest paper-faithful refinement is simply to make the ambient space, the cover notation, and the quantifier over all finite powers explicit. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=4751a09b2173c9726c9936b8b6ae7acd3ae230b3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
